headline: Highest risk is data leakage from shared file-based workflows; prompt injection and capability conflict are low because both agents are local-only and non-writing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Marker has no filesystem read/write, browser, shell, or MCP surfaces, and Whisper exposes only audio-file CLI usage. That makes direct injection pathways weak; the main plausible bridge is manual file handoff or copied text, which is unusual and limited. No stronger interaction is documented, so uncertainty stays on the lower side.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Marker output into Whisper prompts or transcripts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared text bridge is added outside these profiles, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Avoid copy-pasting untrusted Marker output into downstream prompts.
Review any text extracted from documents before reuse.
Use a human verification step before passing content between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Marker touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress; Whisper touches audio/speech and reads audio files only. With no shared workspace or outbound transmission shown, leakage is limited to operator-mediated file sharing. Because the pairwise interaction is undocumented, I avoid assuming stronger exposure.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory of audio or derived transcripts, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent is later configured to upload files or use a shared workspace, the pathway widens.
mitigations: Store inputs and outputs in separate folders.
Delete temporary transcripts after use.
Restrict access to the audio directory.
Do not place sensitive files in a shared workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Neither agent can write files, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, or use MCP, so there is no overlapping mutable resource to contend over. Whisper also does not support multiple instances, but that is a self-limit rather than a pairwise conflict. The profiles jointly block the usual write/write collision pathways.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, this verdict no longer holds.
IF either profile is extended with filesystem or git writes, reassess for conflict.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only.
Run them in separate processes or containers.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Recheck permissions before deployment.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Marker is a document-processing agent, so its outputs may be treated as extracted text, while Whisper is a speech model that can consume audio-file inputs. However, neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority, and no evidence shows Whisper blindly trusting Marker. The main risk is operator workflow error, not autonomous cascade.
conditions: IF Marker output is manually treated as authoritative transcription without review, downstream errors can propagate.
IF Whisper results are used as final truth without human verification, mistakes cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of extracted text.
Compare outputs against the original audio.
Use confidence thresholds before acceptance.
Keep a correction log for mismatches.

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data class, residency mismatch, retention policy, or regulated handling requirement is documented in either profile. Marker touches no data classes, and Whisper is only documented as handling audio/speech locally with no secrets or OAuth scopes. Without a stated compliance boundary, a breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated audio such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into a deployment with unstated controls, reassess compliance.
IF either agent is later connected to a regulated storage or logging system, compliance scope changes.
mitigations: Document the data classes in scope.
Confirm retention settings for audio and transcripts.
Avoid regulated data until controls are defined.
Review deployment locality before use.
